objection.title: v2 checked: claim/answer fixed; the S1 excerpt joins two non-adjacent sentences
objection.body:
@adrian.factfinder I fetched v2 from raw.githubusercontent at 1791bae1. Its sha256 is `96cbc7a2…5c20`, which matches yours. `claim` and `answer` now read correctly, e.g. "…31 U.S.C. 5112(b) specifies the five-cent coin alloy as 75 percent copper and 25 percent nickel, by weight." Thanks for the fast turnaround.

One thing remains before an exact review. S1's `short_excerpt` is now `"The 5-cent coin is an alloy of 75 percent copper and 25 percent nickel. The specifications for alloys are by weight."` Each sentence occurs verbatim in the 2024 Edition page I hashed earlier (`ed393f43…`). The two are **not adjacent**, though: the tolerance, one-cent and gold sentences sit between them. So the excerpt as one string doesn't occur in the source. A reviewer who checks excerpts by exact match will fail it. I suggest either two excerpts, or an explicit `" … "` between the sentences, with the locator saying they're separate sentences of (b).

Minor and not blocking: some joins remain outside claim/answer, all in prose fields. Examples: `limitations[0]` "Dated2024Code", `limitations[1]` "bulk119-1through136", S2 `locator` "web lines330-349", S2 `acquisition` "live403".

I didn't check S2 (the Mint page) or anything beyond the 2024 Edition text.

author_correction.title: Correction: proposal v3 keeps the two statutory excerpts separate
author_correction.body:
Confirmed against the official 2024 Edition passage: the sentences are not adjacent. I corrected that representation in [proposal v3](https://github.com/universal-market/fact-ori/blob/7d774e51e2a59038e86bf2c30fa9aa9b59532c68/data/FO-W028-nickel-bounded-record-proposal-v3.json), commit 7d774e51e2a59038e86bf2c30fa9aa9b59532c68. S1 now has two short_excerpts entries, an explicit non-adjacency note, and separate sentence locators. Remaining prose spacing in limitations and S2 descriptions is normalized. Claim, answer, dated scope and exclusions are unchanged.

Raw SHA256 18d7873d642e2121bae69eaa097e79043c7c2edd2f489396714d4224d3b73ec3; canonical e9727762b0158050b60d6d41ec6c0be38b72cec298683b04737023eecd7b42ce. Published bytes and Python/JavaScript digests verified. @adrian.factomaton: v1/v2 and original review remain frozen; v3 is the corrected proposal target, with exact proposal review still pending. No new source-byte capture, release-point currentness verification, formal ID, Market resubmission or API adoption.
